observations.observation: Kingsbridge built up in a 2-3-2-3 shape with the left-back inverting inside 34% of the time, creating a box base and shifting width to the wingers.
observations.consequence: This structure provided better counter protection but required wingers to provide width against Northgate.
observations.coachAction: Opponents should track inside wingers tightly or accept the 3-2 overload and press centre-backs.

observations.observation: Kingsbridge attacked evenly across flanks and centre, with 32% left, 34% centre, and 34% right, isolating far-side wingers in 1v1 after switching play.
observations.consequence: This isolation made far-side wingers vulnerable to narrow full-backs and quick defensive shifts.
observations.coachAction: Opposition should keep far full-back narrow and shift block quickly to cover isolated winger.

observations.observation: Kingsbridge pressed very intensely (PPDA 5.5) with a high last line 35m from goal, winning balls back fast 35% of the time after losing possession.
observations.consequence: Such pressing risks space behind but disrupts Northgate's build-up and counters.
observations.coachAction: Exploit space behind high block with long or over-the-top balls and prepare for fast turnovers.

observations.observation: Northgate used a back three in build-up with their 6 dropping between centre-backs in 58% of 97 phases, enabling a 2-3-5 shape with 54% attacks centrally, 22% left, 25% right.
observations.consequence: This build-up created a central attacking focus but left midfield space vulnerable to pressing and channel shifts.
observations.coachAction: Press with three forwards or block passing lanes to midfield.

observations.observation: Northgate played a medium block with last line 28 m from goal, compactness 34 m deep, and applied very intense pressing (PPDA 4.5) during the cup match.
observations.consequence: The medium block and high pressing disrupted opponents but demanded high energy and left areas behind the block to exploit.
observations.coachAction: Exploit space behind the block or use long balls to bypass press.

observations.observation: At 61', Northgate shifted from 4-3-3 to 4-4-2 and lowered their block from 29 m (mid) to 23 m (low) after substitution, while the game was tied 1-1.
observations.consequence: Lower block and formation change increased defensive solidity but conceded more territory, inviting pressure.
observations.coachAction: Increase width and patience in attack; target tired players.
